Use case: identity-preserve.
Recompose this approved fictional adult man's portrait as a SEATED WAIST-UP MEDIUM SHOT. Preserve his specific face; the change is primarily the framing, supported seated posture, and three-quarter camera view.

Show his entire head, neck, both shoulders, upper arms and torso down to the waist, including the upholstered chair back and armrests. Keep a natural adult head-to-body scale and an understated lean build, without muscular enlargement. He sits comfortably back in the chair, his upper back supported, shoulders naturally open and low. One forearm rests loosely on the armrest; hands are at ease. Avoid an upright rigid formal pose or a forward lean. His head is naturally balanced over his torso, chin level, no sideways head tilt.

The camera is at his eye height and about 45 degrees to his left, producing a clear three-quarter face pointing to the viewer's RIGHT. Both eyes remain visible, the far eye and cheek distinctly narrower in perspective. His head and eyes point toward the SAME person who is seated at his own eye height in front of him, outside the image. Eyes look horizontally along the direction of his face, without glancing upward or back to the camera.

SCENE DIRECTION:
He is settled in this familiar room, watching Zhitong as she finishes speaking. He maintains his own unhurried pace and steady attention. His expression offers little immediate feedback. Convey composure through the comfortable supported body and sustained gaze; preserve the reference's natural brow, eyelids and lip shape. Do not squeeze the eyes, clamp the lips, add a frown or perform a dramatic expression. Keep the original mouth's subtle natural resting separation.

Preserve the recognizable face under perspective: the same eye spacing, brow and eye shapes, nose, lips, cheekbones, jaw width and length, and subtly angular continuous chin. Same youthful ADULT age, pale gray-blue irises, short dark wavy hair, natural skin tone and texture, black shirt and dark textured jacket. Do not narrow or lengthen the face, hollow the cheeks, add a cleft chin, age him or make him boyish.

Use moderate directional window light with readable eye sockets, cheek planes and mouth; sufficient gentle fill to see the face clearly. Preserve the subdued architectural interior and restrained chair styling of the reference. One photorealistic color photograph, vertical 3:4. Only this man in the image. No extra story props, text, collage or watermark.
